summary: Satoshi Naiki works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Kyoto University, where he served as Assistant Professor at the Center for Cultural Heritage Studies (attested 2016–2020).

Satya Swarup Misra was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as Professor and Head of Sanskrit at the University of Lucknow (attested 1958) and Professor of Indology and Linguistics at Banaras Hindu University circa 1976 to 1995.

Satya Vrat Shastri was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Punjabi University (~1949–1953) and Banaras Hindu University (~1953–1956), later holding posts at the University of Delhi (~1955–1995) and Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Satyendra Nath Bose studied at Hindu School (~1907–1909), Presidency University (1909–1915), and UCSTA (1917–1921). He held posts at the University of Dhaka (1921–1947), University of Calcutta (1947–1956), and succeeded Prabodh Chandra Bagchi as Vice-chancellor of Visva-Bharati University (~1956–1958).

Sayadaw U Sīlānanda studied under U Paññāvanta (-1947) and Mahasi Sayadaw (~1952–1982). In Buddhist studies, his posts included abbotships in Myanmar, Chancellor of ITBMU (~1998–2005), and Spiritual Director of the Theravada Buddhist Society of America (~1979–2005).
Sayaka Sonoda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who earned her PhD at Toyo University under the supervision of Shinobu Yamaguchi.

Scott A. Mitchell is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne (attested 2008) and held a post as Professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015).
Scott Dalby is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and served as a lecturer at Amsterdam University College (attested 2014).

Scott Pacey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed his doctorate at Australian National University (to 2011), was a postdoctoral fellow at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and lectured at the University of Manchester (attested 2014).

Sean D. Gaffney specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held a post at SOAS University of London (attested 1996) and earned his PhD there under Tadeusz Skorupski (attested 2003), having also studied under Denwood, Söhnen-Thieme, Piatigorsky, and Seyfort Ruegg.
See Mui Yian is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the doctoral supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).
Seema Alavi is a historian and Indologist. She studied at the University of Cambridge (~1986–1991) and held academic posts at the University of Delhi (~1994–2021) and Ashoka University (~2021).

Seigai Omura was a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Tokyo University of the Arts (~1889–1893) and served as a professor at Tokyo School of Fine Arts (~1898–1927).

Seiichi Mizuno specialized in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1926 to 1929 and later served there as a professor from circa 1949 to 1968.

Seiichiro Ono worked in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1914–1917) and later held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1918–1952) and Aichi Gakuin University (~1952–1972).

Seiji Kimura works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and held posts there (attested 1990) and as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995).
Seiji Kumagai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Kyoto University (~2003–2008) and was appointed an associate professor there circa 2013.
Seiji Nemoto specializes in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Meiji University (~1968–1978) and served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba (~2000–2015).
Seijun Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from circa 1977 to 1986, later becoming a professor there circa 1990.
Seiko Hirata was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu (~1946–1950) and held a post at Hanazono University.
